title: Published seasonal earthquake peaks at six western US volcanic areas did not repeat in 2004-2025 ComCat data; more snow gave a larger July-December share at three volcanoes after 2003 only
abstract: Christiansen et al. (2005) and Saar and Manga (2003) reported seasonal earthquake rates at western US volcanic areas in data that ended near 2003. We tested the published peak half-years with USGS ComCat data for Mount St. Helens, Mount Hood, Mammoth Mountain, the Long Valley east south moat, Yellowstone Lake and Hebgen Lake, for 1984-2003 and for new data from 2004-2025, with three non-volcanic control areas. The statistic was the rate ratio of Gardner-Knopoff declustered events in the published peak half-year to the other half. A year-rotation null kept swarms and yearly totals. In 2004-2025 no volcanic area had a higher rate in its published peak half-year (one-sided p 0.07-0.97; Stouffer p = 0.80). In 1984-2003 our method found the signal only at Mammoth Mountain (rate ratio 1.39, p = 0.019, peak near 31 August), and it did not continue (0.88, 95% CI 0.61-1.35). A small late-August excess at Mount St. Helens disappeared for larger events and agrees with seasonal detection change. In 2004-2025, years with more 1 April snow water equivalent had a larger July-December share at Mount St. Helens, Mount Hood and Mammoth Mountain (permutation p 0.010-0.041; six-area Stouffer p = 0.009), but not in 1984-2003 or in control areas. Limitations: our own area boundaries, a live catalogue, few snow stations, and many related tests without adjustment.
